The Guardian: Torrential rain causes widespread damage; Typhoon Soudel dumped torrential rain in southeastern China's Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces last week, while north-western South Africa faced thunderstorms and oppressive heat in the central-southern US. The city of Putian in Fujian province recorded 416.5 mm of rain in the 24-hour period between Thursday and Friday, while surrounding villages recorded more than 500 mm during the same period. In Fujian, officials estimate that nearly 600,000 people have been evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. Another 128,000 people in 53 counties across Jiangxi were also affected, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people. Flooding, landslides and damage to infrastructure have been widely reported in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in Wenzhou's Zhejiang city on Wednesday after heavy rains caused flooding in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed Thursday, leveling 100 houses.
